downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.detail: ICM42688P and LSM6DSO were added to the accelerometer hardware list after 4.2.11, so 4.2.11 rejects those names.
downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.note: 4.2.11 has no accelerometer option for this chip and nothing equivalent, so the setting goes back to AUTO. After flashing, check that the accelerometer is detected. If it isn't, 4.2.11 may not support your board's sensor.

downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 removed the 1000 offset from the smooth I-term accelerator, changing 0.01*(gain - 1000) to 0.01*gain so that 0 means off, and used the same gain for a new P boost. STEP mode reads the gain the same way in both versions.
downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-downgrade.note: In SMOOTH mode, 4.2.11 counts the anti-gravity gain from 1000 (1000 means off), so 1000 was added to your value to keep the same I-term boost. In STEP mode the value carries over unchanged, but it is raised to 4.2.11's minimum of 1000. The extra P boost on throttle chops that 4.3.2 drives from this gain doesn't exist in 4.2.11.

downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-smooth-zero-.detail: 4.2's SMOOTH I boost uses 0.01 × (gain − 1000). 4.3 removed the 1000 offset so that 0 means off, and also used the same gain to drive a new P boost on throttle chops (not on yaw). The default is 3500 in both versions.
downgrade:anti-gravity-gain-smooth-zero-.note: In SMOOTH mode, Betaflight 4.2 counts this gain from 1000 (1000 means off), so the converter added 1000 to keep your I boost the same (e.g. 4000 becomes 5000, 0 becomes 1000). 4.2 has no extra P boost on throttle chops, so anti-gravity will feel somewhat weaker. In STEP mode your number is kept, raised to 4.2's minimum of 1000 if it was lower.

downgrade:baro-hardware-dps310-reset.detail: Support for the Infineon DPS310 barometer, including its entry in the baro_hardware list, was added in 4.3. 4.2.11 has no equivalent.
downgrade:baro-hardware-dps310-reset.note: 4.2.11 has no DPS310 barometer option, so the board's own default barometer setting is used instead. Your DPS310 can't be selected in 4.2.11, so don't count on barometer readings after the downgrade.

downgrade:blackbox-disable-alt-removed.note: 4.2.11 cannot switch this field off, so it is always logged. If you had it disabled in 4.3.2, expect it in your logs again.

downgrade:blackbox-disable-rc-removed.detail: 4.3 adds an opt-out for RC-command logging whose default OFF matches the 4.2 behaviour, so only a value of ON cannot be expressed in 4.2.11.
downgrade:blackbox-disable-rc-removed.note: 4.2.11 always logs RC commands and has no way to turn that off. If this was ON in 4.3.2, that choice is lost and RC data will appear in your logs again.

downgrade:blackbox-disable-rssi-removed.detail: 4.3 adds an opt-out for RSSI logging whose default OFF matches the 4.2 behaviour, so only a value of ON has no equivalent in 4.2.11.
downgrade:blackbox-disable-rssi-removed.note: 4.2.11 logs RSSI whenever RSSI is configured and has no way to turn that off. If this was ON in 4.3.2, that choice is lost and RSSI will appear in your logs again.

downgrade:blackbox-disable-setpoint-remo.detail: 4.3 adds an opt-out for setpoint logging whose default OFF matches the 4.2 behaviour, so only a value of ON cannot be carried to 4.2.11.
downgrade:blackbox-disable-setpoint-remo.note: 4.2.11 always logs setpoint and has no way to turn that off. If this was ON in 4.3.2, that choice is lost and setpoint will appear in your logs again.

downgrade:blackbox-record-acc-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the single blackbox_record_acc switch with per-field blackbox selection, later reworked into a mask of disabled fields. That mask gives blackbox_disable_acc, which is the inverse of the old setting.
downgrade:blackbox-record-acc-downgrade.note: In 4.2.11, accelerometer logging is controlled by blackbox_record_acc, which works the opposite way round to blackbox_disable_acc. Your choice was carried over: if accelerometer logging was on, blackbox_record_acc is ON, and if it was off, it is OFF.

downgrade:blackbox-sample-rate-removed.detail: 4.3's blackbox_sample_rate logs a fixed fraction of the PID loop (1/1 to 1/16). 4.2's blackbox_p_ratio gives a rate in Hz that depends on the loop rate, so converting between them needs the PID loop frequency.
downgrade:blackbox-sample-rate-removed.note: Betaflight 4.2 sets the logging rate with blackbox_p_ratio instead. The converter can't tell your PID loop rate, so 4.2's default of 32 (1 kHz logging) applies. To keep your old rate, set blackbox_p_ratio to 32 × PID loop rate in kHz × your fraction, e.g. 1/2 on an 8 kHz loop: `set blackbox_p_ratio = 128`.

downgrade:blackbox-sample-rate-removed-2.detail: 4.3 gives the logging rate as a fraction of the PID loop rate; 4.2.11 logs at blackbox_p_ratio / 32 kHz (32 = 1 kHz) whatever the loop rate. Converting needs the PID loop frequency, so no value is carried over.
downgrade:blackbox-sample-rate-removed-2.note: 4.2.11 logs at the rate set by blackbox_p_ratio instead, and its default value of 32 now applies. If you want a different logging rate, set blackbox_p_ratio yourself with `set blackbox_p_ratio = <value>`.

downgrade:crsf-use-rx-snr-rssi-percent-b.detail: When this is ON, 4.3 also works out the CRSF RSSI percentage from uplink SNR ((SNR + 10) × 20, clamped), so -10 dB maps to 0. 4.2 uses SNR only in place of RSSI dBm.
downgrade:crsf-use-rx-snr-rssi-percent-b.note: In Betaflight 4.2, ON only replaces the RSSI dBm value with SNR. The RSSI percentage still comes from the Crossfire RSSI. You don't need to do anything unless you relied on an SNR-based RSSI %.

downgrade:d-max-gain-renamed.detail: The CLI name changed but the field is the same, with the same 0-100 range and default of 37. The boost logic behind it was re-tuned in 4.3.
downgrade:d-max-gain-renamed.note: Betaflight 4.2 calls this d_min_boost_gain and tunes the D boost differently: for the same gyro or stick activity, the same number raises D toward its full value about twice as much, and the boost rises and falls more slowly. The converter kept your number. If D feels too high in propwash, lower d_min_boost_gain.

downgrade:d-min-pitch-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the d_min_pitch maximum from 100 to 250 when the tuning sliders were added. The setting's meaning did not change, so only values above 100 can't be represented in 4.2.11.
downgrade:d-min-pitch-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 only accepts d_min_pitch values up to 100 (4.3.2 allows up to 250), so anything higher was lowered to 100. Values of 100 or less carry over unchanged. If yours was lowered, you'll have less minimum D than before, so check your tune.

downgrade:d-min-roll-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the d_min_roll maximum from 100 to 250 when the tuning sliders were added. The setting's meaning and the way it is used in flight did not change, so only values above 100 can't be represented in 4.2.11.
downgrade:d-min-roll-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 only accepts d_min_roll values up to 100 (4.3.2 allows up to 250), so anything higher was lowered to 100. Values of 100 or less carry over unchanged. If yours was lowered, you'll have less minimum D than before, so check your tune.

downgrade:d-min-yaw-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the d_min_yaw maximum from 100 to 250 when the tuning sliders were added. The setting's meaning and the way it is used in flight did not change, so only values above 100 can't be represented in 4.2.11.
downgrade:d-min-yaw-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 only accepts d_min_yaw values up to 100 (4.3.2 allows up to 250), so anything higher was lowered to 100. Values of 100 or less carry over unchanged, including the default of 0.

downgrade:d-pitch-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the PID gain maximum from 200 to 250 when tuning slider support was added. The gain means the same thing in both versions. Only the upper limit differs.
downgrade:d-pitch-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 allows D gains only up to 200, so a pitch D above 200 is lowered to 200 and anything else carries over unchanged. If your tune relied on more pitch D than 200, check how the quad flies after the downgrade.

downgrade:d-roll-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the PID gain maximum from 200 to 250 when tuning slider support was added. The gain means the same thing in both versions. Only the upper limit differs.
downgrade:d-roll-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 allows D gains only up to 200, so a roll D above 200 is lowered to 200 and anything else carries over unchanged. If your tune relied on more roll D than 200, check how the quad flies after the downgrade.

downgrade:d-yaw-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 raised the PID gain maximum from 200 to 250 when tuning slider support was added. The gain means the same thing in both versions. Only the upper limit differs.
downgrade:d-yaw-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 allows D gains only up to 200, so a yaw D above 200 is lowered to 200 and anything else carries over unchanged.

downgrade:debug-mode-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 renamed FF_INTERPOLATED and FF_LIMIT in place to FEEDFORWARD and FEEDFORWARD_LIMIT during its feedforward rework. 4.3.2 also added several debug modes that 4.2.11 does not have.
downgrade:debug-mode-downgrade.note: The two feedforward debug modes have different names in 4.2.11: FEEDFORWARD becomes FF_INTERPOLATED and FEEDFORWARD_LIMIT becomes FF_LIMIT. They log the same thing, so nothing needs doing.

downgrade:debug-mode-new-names-reset.detail: 4.3 added these debug modes along with new features such as ExpressLRS SPI receivers, GHST debugging, scheduler timing tracking, D-term lowpass debugging and the Tramp VTX rework.
downgrade:debug-mode-new-names-reset.note: This debug mode was added in 4.3 and has no counterpart in 4.2.11, so the board's default debug mode is used instead. It only changes what extra data is recorded for tuning and troubleshooting. If you need debug data in your logs, pick one of the 4.2.11 modes, e.g. `set debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED`.

downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-downgra.detail: 4.3.2 added UART9 and USART10 as port identifiers 8 and 9, and moved LPUART1 from 8 to 40. In 4.2.11, port 8 is LPUART1, which exists only on the NUCLEOH743, and the highest identifier is 31.
downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-downgra.note: Port numbers 8 and 9 (UART9 and USART10) and 40 (LPUART1) don't exist in 4.2.11, so a value on one of those ports becomes -1 (none) and MSP DisplayPort is off. Any other port number keeps its meaning and is kept. If it became -1, pick a port the board has in 4.2.11 and set it with `set displayport_msp_serial = <port>`.

downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-lpuart1.detail: In 4.3.2 the serial port numbers changed: LPUART1 moved from 8 to 40, and 8 and 9 went to the new UART9 and USART10. Betaflight 4.2.11 allows port numbers only up to 31 and has LPUART1 only on one development board.
downgrade:displayport-msp-serial-lpuart1.note: Your HD OSD link (MSP DisplayPort) was on LPUART1, port 40 in 4.3.2. Betaflight 4.2.11 has no LPUART1 on this flight controller, so MSP DisplayPort is set to no port (-1) and the HD OSD won't show. Wire the HD video link to another UART, then point the setting at that port with `set displayport_msp_serial = <port number>`.

downgrade:dma-spi-mosi-miso-names-droppe.detail: 4.3.2 renamed SPI_TX/SPI_RX to SPI_MOSI/SPI_MISO but still accepts the old names, so it prints each SPI DMA option twice. 4.2.11 rejects the new names.
downgrade:dma-spi-mosi-miso-names-droppe.note: 4.2.11 only knows the SPI DMA options by their older names, SPI_TX and SPI_RX. A 4.3.2 config lists each SPI DMA option under both names with the same value, so the SPI_TX or SPI_RX line carries your setting and normally you have nothing to do.

downgrade:dterm-lowpass-hz-downgrade.detail: In 4.3 this setting was renamed to dterm_lpf1_static_hz to give the gyro and D-term filters consistent names, and its maximum dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz. That means every 4.3.2 value fits within the 4.2.11 range of 0-4000.
downgrade:dterm-lowpass-hz-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 uses the older name dterm_lowpass_hz for the static D-term lowpass 1 cutoff. It means the same thing, so your cutoff carries over unchanged.

downgrade:dterm-lowpass-type-pt2-pt3-fal.detail: PT2 and PT3 were added in 4.3.2, and dterm_lpf1_type was named dterm_lowpass_type before that. Betaflight sets all three PT types to -3 dB at the cutoff, but past the cutoff PT1 rolls off at 20 dB per decade, PT2 at 40 and PT3 at 60.
downgrade:dterm-lowpass-type-pt2-pt3-fal.note: 4.2.11 offers only PT1 and BIQUAD for the first D-term lowpass filter. PT1 and BIQUAD carry over unchanged. PT2 or PT3 becomes PT1, which filters less above the cutoff (with less delay), so if you used either one, check your D-term filtering before flying.

downgrade:dterm-lowpass2-hz-downgrade.detail: 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass2_hz to dterm_lpf2_static_hz without changing what it does. 4.3.2 also lowered the maximum from 4000 to 1000 Hz, so any 4.3.2 value fits within 4.2.11's range.
downgrade:dterm-lowpass2-hz-downgrade.note: This is the same second D-term lowpass filter cutoff under its 4.2.11 name. Your value carries over unchanged, so nothing needs doing.

downgrade:dterm-lowpass2-type-pt2-pt3-fa.detail: PT2 and PT3 were added in 4.3.2, and dterm_lpf2_type was named dterm_lowpass2_type before that. Betaflight sets all three PT types to -3 dB at the cutoff, but past the cutoff PT1 rolls off at 20 dB per decade, PT2 at 40 and PT3 at 60.
downgrade:dterm-lowpass2-type-pt2-pt3-fa.note: 4.2.11 offers only PT1 and BIQUAD for the second D-term lowpass filter. PT1 and BIQUAD carry over unchanged. PT2 or PT3 becomes PT1, which filters less above the cutoff (with less delay), so if you used either one, check your D-term filtering before flying.

downgrade:dterm-lpf1-type-renamed-from-d.detail: 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass_type to dterm_lpf1_type and added PT2 and PT3 to the list of lowpass types. 4.2.11 only has PT1 and BIQUAD.
downgrade:dterm-lpf1-type-renamed-from-d.note: In 4.2.11 the first D-term lowpass filter type uses its older name, dterm_lowpass_type. PT1 and BIQUAD carry over unchanged. PT2 and PT3 don't exist there and become PT1, which filters less above the cutoff.

downgrade:dterm-lpf2-type-renamed-from-d.detail: 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass2_type to dterm_lpf2_type and added PT2 and PT3 to the list of lowpass types. 4.2.11 only has PT1 and BIQUAD.
downgrade:dterm-lpf2-type-renamed-from-d.note: In 4.2.11 the second D-term lowpass filter type uses its older name, dterm_lowpass2_type. PT1 and BIQUAD carry over unchanged. PT2 and PT3 don't exist there and become PT1, which filters less above the cutoff.

downgrade:dyn-idle-d-gain-removed.detail: Commit 8050ecd1e77a replaced the 4.2 integrating-P idle controller with a P/I/D dynamic idle controller, which added dyn_idle_d_gain.
downgrade:dyn-idle-d-gain-removed.note: 4.2.11 has a different dynamic idle controller with no D term, so no value carries over. Its own idle settings (idle_adjustment_speed, idle_p, idle_pid_limit) stay at their 4.2.11 defaults. If you tuned dynamic idle, check idle behaviour after flashing.

downgrade:dyn-idle-i-gain-removed.detail: Commit 8050ecd1e77a replaced the 4.2 integrating-P idle controller with a P/I/D dynamic idle controller, which added dyn_idle_i_gain.
downgrade:dyn-idle-i-gain-removed.note: 4.2.11 has a different dynamic idle controller with no I gain, so no value carries over. Its own idle settings (idle_adjustment_speed, idle_p, idle_pid_limit) stay at their 4.2.11 defaults. If you tuned dynamic idle, check idle behaviour after flashing.

downgrade:dyn-idle-min-rpm-downgrade.detail: In 4.3 idle_min_rpm was renamed to dyn_idle_min_rpm, and a later change raised its maximum from 100 to 200 without changing the units. Values from 101 to 200 have no equivalent in 4.2.11.
downgrade:dyn-idle-min-rpm-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 calls this idle_min_rpm, with the same units and meaning, so your dynamic idle minimum carries over. 4.2.11 only accepts 0-100, so a value above 100 is lowered to 100. That gives a lower idle speed than you had.

downgrade:dyn-idle-p-gain-removed.detail: Commit 8050ecd1e77a turned the 4.2 integrating-P idle controller (idle_adjustment_speed, idle_p, idle_pid_limit) into a P/I/D controller with separate gains.
downgrade:dyn-idle-p-gain-removed.note: 4.2.11 has a different dynamic idle controller, so this gain has no matching setting and the 4.2.11 defaults apply. If you tuned dynamic idle, check idle behaviour after flashing and adjust idle_p and the other idle settings there.

downgrade:dyn-notch-min-hz-downgrade.detail: 4.3 lowered the minimum of dyn_notch_min_hz from 60 to 20 Hz and moved it into a new dynamic notch settings group. Its meaning didn't change.
downgrade:dyn-notch-min-hz-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 doesn't accept a dynamic notch minimum below 60 Hz, so a value from 20 to 59 is raised to 60. Any other value carries over unchanged.

downgrade:expresslrs-spi-receiver-settin.detail: PR #10788 added ExpressLRS support, and PR #11229 and PR #11380 later changed how the receiver is handled.
downgrade:expresslrs-spi-receiver-settin.note: 4.2.11 can't run an ExpressLRS receiver built into the flight controller (support arrived in 4.3), so these settings are dropped and such a receiver won't link on 4.2.11. Write down your UID and rate if you'll go back to 4.3.

downgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed.detail: In 4.3.2 the stage-2 guard time is failsafe_delay x 100 ms with a 200 ms minimum, which the developers changed to match the failsafe documentation. 4.2.11 still uses 200 ms + failsafe_delay x 100 ms.
downgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed.note: The number is kept, but Betaflight 4.2.11 adds a fixed 200 ms to failsafe_delay x 100 ms, so failsafe stage 2 starts 200 ms later than it did in 4.3.2 (e.g. 10 gives 1.2 s instead of 1.0 s). For the same timing as before, lower the value by 2.

downgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-kept.detail: In 4.3.2 the recovery time is failsafe_recovery_delay x 100 ms with a 200 ms minimum, and it applies to every way of entering failsafe. 4.2.11 uses 200 ms + failsafe_recovery_delay x 100 ms, and some of its failsafe paths use fixed times.
downgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-kept.note: The number is kept, but Betaflight 4.2.11 adds a fixed 200 ms to failsafe_recovery_delay x 100 ms, so recovery from failsafe takes 200 ms longer than in 4.3.2 (e.g. 30 gives 3.2 s instead of 3.0 s). For the same timing as before, lower the value by 2 (no lower than 0). Some ways out of failsafe in 4.2.11 use fixed times instead of this delay.

downgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-remo.detail: This setting was introduced and renamed during the 4.3 cycle, as seen in commits 636d563abe31 and 5ca7ea8f4b69.
downgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-remo.note: There is no setting in 4.2.11 to put this value into, so 4.2.11 keeps its own feedforward behaviour. If you tuned feedforward jitter, check how feedforward feels after flashing.

downgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-downgrade.detail: 4.3 replaced ff_interpolate_sp with feedforward_averaging and changed the averaging count from the ff_interpolate_sp value to feedforward_averaging + 1. So ON in 4.2.11 matches OFF in 4.3.2, and AVERAGED_N matches N_POINT.
downgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 sets feedforward averaging with ff_interpolate_sp, and its option names are shifted by one: OFF becomes ON (no averaging), and 2_POINT, 3_POINT and 4_POINT become AVERAGED_2, AVERAGED_3 and AVERAGED_4. Feedforward behaves the same as before.

downgrade:frsky-unit-downgrade.detail: 4.3 rebuilt the internal unit list to match the labels (IMPERIAL converts, the others send raw data) and added BRITISH. In 4.2.11, the default label IMPERIAL actually sent raw metric data.
downgrade:frsky-unit-downgrade.note: In 4.2.11 this setting's labels work the opposite way to their names: IMPERIAL sends the raw metric data and METRIC applies the conversion. downgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped.detail: In 4.2.11 the IMPERIAL label sends raw metric data and METRIC applies the (x-32)/1.8 conversion. The 4.3 commit that added measurement units for the OSD and FrSky hub telemetry lined the code up with the labels and added BRITISH, which sends raw data.
downgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped.note: Nothing to do. downgrade:gps-ublox-galileo-apply-change.detail: Commit 2f89cf3 (M9N support, in 4.3) changed the u-blox setup: 4.3 reads the receiver's GNSS config and sets only the Galileo flag on a default M8N. 4.2 builds and writes a complete GNSS config block.

downgrade:gyro-hardware-lpf-bmi-osr-rese.detail: 4.3 added OPTION_1 and OPTION_2 to choose the oversampling (OSR) mode on BMI gyros, which changes the gyro's built-in lowpass filter cutoffs. 4.2.11 offers only NORMAL and EXPERIMENTAL.
downgrade:gyro-hardware-lpf-bmi-osr-rese.note: 4.2.11 doesn't have the OPTION_1 and OPTION_2 BMI gyro filter modes, so the gyro's hardware lowpass goes back to `set gyro_hardware_lpf = NORMAL`. downgrade:gyro-lowpass2-hz-downgrade.detail: In 4.3 this setting was renamed to gyro_lpf2_static_hz to give the gyro and D-term filters consistent names, and its maximum dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz. That means every 4.3.2 value fits within the 4.2.11 range of 0-4000.

downgrade:rates-type-default-changed.detail: 4.3.2 changed the default rates_type from BETAFLIGHT to ACTUAL, with a soft centre feel. The rate types and what they mean are the same in both versions.
downgrade:rates-type-default-changed.note: Betaflight 4.2.11's default rates are BETAFLIGHT, not ACTUAL, and its default rate curve is different too. The converter kept your rates so your stick feel stays the same. To try 4.2.11's defaults, use `set rates_type = BETAFLIGHT` and set your rate values again to suit.

downgrade:rc-interp-downgrade.detail: 4.3 removed RC interpolation. 'No RC smoothing', which 4.2 expressed as rc_interp OFF with rc_smoothing_type INTERPOLATION, became rc_smoothing = OFF in 4.3.
downgrade:rc-interp-downgrade.note: 4.3.2 has no RC interpolation, so this value comes from your rc_smoothing setting. It is OFF if RC smoothing was off. Otherwise it is AUTO, the 4.2.11 default, which does nothing while rc_smoothing_type is FILTER.

downgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-factor-remov.detail: The RC smoothing rework replaced rc_smoothing_auto_smoothness with a separate rc_smoothing_auto_factor, and PT2/PT3 filter maths changed how the auto cutoff is calculated and widened the range from 0-50 to 0-250. No conversion formula between the two scales is known.
downgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-factor-remov.note: 4.2.11's setting is rc_smoothing_auto_smoothness (0-50, default 10), on a different scale from this one (0-250, default 30). Nothing is converted, so 4.2.11's default applies. If you want a different RC smoothing feel, set rc_smoothing_auto_smoothness yourself and test it.

downgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-factor-throt.detail: The RC smoothing rework split the single smoothness factor into a roll/pitch/yaw factor and a separate throttle factor, and PT2/PT3 filter maths changed the auto-cutoff calculation and widened the range from 0-50 to 0-250. No conversion formula is known.
downgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-factor-throt.note: 4.2.11 has a single rc_smoothing_auto_smoothness setting for RC smoothing, with a different scale, and nothing is converted from this throttle value. 4.2.11 uses its own default; if you want a different feel, set rc_smoothing_auto_smoothness yourself and test it.

downgrade:rc-smoothing-input-hz-downgrad.detail: 4.3 split the single input cutoff into rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff and rc_smoothing_throttle_cutoff, and both keep 0 as automatic. Going back to 4.2 merges them into one again.
downgrade:rc-smoothing-input-hz-downgrad.note: 4.2.11 has a single RC smoothing input cutoff, not separate setpoint and throttle cutoffs. It takes your rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff value. If your rc_smoothing_throttle_cutoff was different, that value is lost. 0 still means automatic.

downgrade:rc-smoothing-throttle-cutoff-d.detail: In 4.3, throttle got its own cutoff (0 = auto), split off from the old single input cutoff, and the rc_interp_ch channel mask was removed. Going back to 4.2.11, the single input cutoff can hold only one value, and the setpoint cutoff is the one kept.
downgrade:rc-smoothing-throttle-cutoff-d.note: 4.2.11 has no separate throttle smoothing cutoff, so this value is lost. 4.2.11 has a single RC smoothing cutoff, rc_smoothing_input_hz, which takes your setpoint cutoff value, and it also filters throttle when rc_interp_ch includes throttle.

downgrade:rc-smoothing-type-downgrade.detail: 4.3 removed RC interpolation and replaced rc_smoothing_type (INTERPOLATION/FILTER) with an OFF/ON rc_smoothing switch, where ON means the filter. 4.2's way of having no RC smoothing, INTERPOLATION with rc_interp OFF, is what 4.3 calls OFF.
downgrade:rc-smoothing-type-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 picks an RC smoothing type instead of an on/off switch. If your RC smoothing was on, you get FILTER, the same filter you used in 4.3.2. If it was off, you get INTERPOLATION with rc_interp = OFF, which is how 4.2.11 turns RC smoothing off.

downgrade:rpm-filter-min-hz-downgrade.detail: In 4.3, gyro_rpm_notch_min was renamed to rpm_filter_min_hz and its lower limit dropped from 50 Hz to 30 Hz. The default stayed at 100.
downgrade:rpm-filter-min-hz-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 calls this setting gyro_rpm_notch_min, with the same meaning in Hz, so your value carries over. Values below 50 are raised to 50, the lowest value 4.2.11 accepts.

downgrade:rx-spi-protocol-new-protocols-.detail: 4.3 added EXPRESSLRS, FRSKY_X_V2 and FRSKY_X_LBT_V2 to the SPI receiver protocol list. None of them exists in 4.2.11, and nothing there does the same job.
downgrade:rx-spi-protocol-new-protocols-.note: The built-in SPI receiver in 4.2.11 doesn't support this protocol, so the board's default protocol applies. Your receiver may not link with your transmitter, so check the link carefully before flying.

downgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered.detail: 4.3 renumbered LPUART1 from port 8 to port 40 when it added UART9 and USART10. In 4.2, LPUART1 was port 8 and existed only on the NUCLEOH743 development board, so 4.2.11 rejects a `serial 40` line.
downgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered.note: Betaflight 4.2.11 has no LPUART1 on H743 or G4 flight controllers, so whatever this port was used for (the functions number after the port) is not set on any port now. Before flying, assign those functions to another free UART with the `serial` command, and check that the device on LPUART1 is wired to that UART.

downgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered-drop.detail: Betaflight 4.3 renumbered the serial ports: LPUART1 went from 8 to 40, and 8 and 9 became UART9 and USART10. 4.2.11 has no port 40, and it only lists LPUART1, as port 8, on NUCLEOH743 builds, so these ports can't be carried back.
downgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered-drop.note: This port has no equivalent in 4.2.11, so whatever it was set up for (receiver, telemetry, VTX control, GPS, MSP and so on) won't work after the downgrade. If you need those functions, move them to a UART that 4.2.11 has on your board with a `serial` line, and check that the device is wired to that UART.

downgrade:serialrx-provider-ghst-reset.detail: GHST support was added in 4.3 as a new entry at the end of the serial receiver protocol list, in a commit with no PR number. 4.2.11's list stops at SRXL2, so there is no equivalent value.
downgrade:serialrx-provider-ghst-reset.note: 4.2.11 has no GHST receiver protocol, so the board's default protocol applies and a GHST receiver won't talk to the flight controller. If your receiver can output a protocol 4.2.11 supports, set it with `set serialrx_provider = <name>` (for example `set serialrx_provider = CRSF`), and check the receiver responds before flying.

downgrade:stats-downgrade.detail: In 4.3, the on/off stats switch and the fixed minimum flight time were merged into stats_min_armed_time_s, where -1 means off and 0 to 127 means on with that minimum armed time in seconds.
downgrade:stats-downgrade.note: 4.2.11 has a simple on/off switch for flight statistics, with a fixed 10-second minimum flight time. Stats come out ON if your 4.3.2 minimum armed time was 0 or more, and OFF if it was -1. A custom minimum time other than 10 seconds can't be kept.

downgrade:stats-min-armed-time-s-downgra.detail: In 4.3, stats_min_armed_time_s replaced 4.2's stats switch and its hard-coded minimum flight time: -1 disables stats, and 0 to 127 enables them with that minimum armed time in seconds.
downgrade:stats-min-armed-time-s-downgra.note: 4.2.11 has only an on/off switch for flight statistics, with a fixed 10-second minimum flight time. Your value becomes `set stats = ON` if it was 0 or more, or `set stats = OFF` if it was -1. A custom minimum time other than 10 seconds can't be kept.

downgrade:stats-min-armed-time-to-stats-.detail: In 4.3.2, stats_min_armed_time_s replaced the stats ON/OFF switch and 4.2.11's fixed 10-second minimum. A value of -1 turns stats off, and 0 or more sets the minimum armed time in seconds.
downgrade:stats-min-armed-time-to-stats-.note: Betaflight 4.2.11 has no minimum armed time for flight stats. Stats are just ON or OFF, and a flight counts once it lasts a fixed 10 seconds. The converter turned stats ON, so flights count after 10 seconds instead of your chosen time. You only need to do something if that matters to you.

downgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-bit.detail: 4.3 added a 'capacity used' sensor as bit 20 and changed how FrSky telemetry reports fuel. 4.2 only knows bits 0-19, so bit 20 is dropped to fit 4.2's maximum of 1048575.
downgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-bit.note: In Betaflight 4.2 the SmartPort Fuel sensor reports mAh drawn, not percent remaining, and there is no separate 'capacity used' sensor. If your radio shows or announces Fuel as a percentage, change that telemetry sensor's unit to mAh.

downgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-dow.detail: In 4.3, a new 'capacity used' sensor was added as bit 20, raising the maximum from 1048575 to 2097151, and it is disabled by default. 4.2.11 accepts only bits 0 to 19, so bit 20 is removed.
downgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-dow.note: The 'capacity used' telemetry sensor (value 1048576) doesn't exist in 4.2.11, so it is dropped from your value. Every other sensor keeps the enabled or disabled state you set.

downgrade:thrust-linear-downgrade.detail: In 4.3 the thrust linearization formula changed to a (1-x)^2 boost with throttle compensation, the maximum went from 100 to 150, and the setting became per PID profile. A least-squares fit of the two curves over the motor range found that a 4.3 value is about 1.8 times the 4.2 value.
downgrade:thrust-linear-downgrade.note: A given thrust_linear value gives a stronger motor boost in 4.3.2 than in 4.2.11, so your value was divided by 1.8 to give about the same boost. The curves have different shapes, so the feel is close but not identical. 4.2.11 uses one value for every PID profile, taken from PID profile 1. If your other profiles used different values, those values are not carried over.

downgrade:thrust-linear-formula-rescaled.detail: 4.3 replaced the curve with a (1 - motor)^2 boost plus throttle compensation, raised the maximum from 100 to 150 and made the setting per PID profile. The 1.8 factor is a least-squares fit between the two curves over the motor range.
downgrade:thrust-linear-formula-rescaled.note: Betaflight 4.2 uses a different thrust-linearization curve: the same number gives about twice the effect, and the maximum is 100. The value was converted approximately (4.3 value / 1.8, capped at 100, e.g. 72 -> 40), taken from PID profile 1, because 4.2 has one value for all PID profiles and no low-throttle throttle boost. Test-fly and adjust.

upgrade:anti-gravity-smooth-gain-rezeroe.detail: The I-term boost changed from 0.01 × (gain − 1000) to 0.01 × gain, so 'off' moved from 1000 to 0 and the range now starts at 0. The same gain now also scales a P boost that 4.2.11 did not have.
upgrade:anti-gravity-smooth-gain-rezeroe.note: In SMOOTH anti-gravity mode, 4.3.2 counts the gain from 0 instead of 1000, so 1000 was subtracted to keep the same I-term boost. STEP mode values carry over unchanged. In 4.3.2 the gain also scales a new P boost on throttle chops, so anti-gravity may feel a little different in flight.

upgrade:anti-gravity-smooth-zero-point-m.detail: In 4.2.11 the SMOOTH I-term boost was computed from (gain - 1000). In 4.3.2 it uses the gain directly, and the same gain also scales a new P boost on throttle chops (not on yaw). STEP mode reads the gain the same way in both versions.
upgrade:anti-gravity-smooth-zero-point-m.note: In SMOOTH anti-gravity mode, 4.3 no longer subtracts 1000 from the gain, and 0 now means off. Your value was lowered by 1000 so the I-term boost stays the same (e.g. 5000 becomes 4000, and 1000, which was off, becomes 0). 4.3 also adds a P boost on quick throttle changes, driven by the same gain, so anti-gravity may still feel somewhat stronger than in 4.2.11.

upgrade:blackbox-p-ratio-needs-pid-loop-.detail: In 4.2.11 the logging rate was blackbox_p_ratio / 32 kHz whatever the loop rate. In 4.3.2 the P-frame interval is 1 << blackbox_sample_rate PID loops (1/1 to 1/16), so converting needs the PID loop frequency, which a dump doesn't hold. A value of 0 (I-frames only) has no direct equivalent.
upgrade:blackbox-p-ratio-needs-pid-loop-.note: 4.3 sets the logging rate with blackbox_sample_rate, a fraction of the PID loop rate, instead of blackbox_p_ratio. The converter can't tell your PID loop rate, so 4.3's default of 1/4 applies. To keep your old rate (blackbox_p_ratio / 32 kHz, e.g. 64 = 2 kHz), divide it by your PID loop rate: 2 kHz on an 8 kHz loop is `set blackbox_sample_rate = 1/4`, on a 4 kHz loop `set blackbox_sample_rate = 1/2`.

upgrade:blackbox-p-ratio-removed.detail: The old setting was a ratio whose logging rate in Hz depended on the PID loop rate. It was replaced by blackbox_sample_rate, a fraction of the PID loop rate, and a dump does not contain the loop rate needed to convert.
upgrade:blackbox-p-ratio-removed.note: Your old logging rate is not carried over, so 4.3.2 uses its default of 1/4. If you want a different blackbox logging rate, set blackbox_sample_rate yourself.

upgrade:blackbox-record-acc-inverted.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the single record switch with a blackbox field-selection mask, where blackbox_disable_acc = ON means the accelerometer is not logged.
upgrade:blackbox-record-acc-inverted.note: Accelerometer logging is now turned off with blackbox_disable_acc instead of turned on with blackbox_record_acc, so your choice was carried over with the opposite value. ACC is logged or not logged just as before.

upgrade:crsf-snr-now-drives-rssi-percent.detail: In 4.3.2, with this setting ON the CRSF RSSI percentage is derived from uplink SNR as (SNR+10)*20, clamped, so -10 dB reads 0 and 0 dB reads 20. The setting is still OFF/ON with default OFF.
upgrade:crsf-snr-now-drives-rssi-percent.note: With this ON, 4.3 also works out the RSSI percentage from the Crossfire link's signal-to-noise ratio, where 4.2 only replaced the RSSI dBm value. The RSSI % on the OSD and the low-RSSI warning now follow SNR. You don't need to do anything unless you relied on the old RSSI %.

upgrade:d-min-boost-gain-renamed-d-max-g.detail: The CLI name changed to d_max_gain on the same field, with the same range (0-100) and default (37). The boost's filtering was also changed, which makes it respond faster.
upgrade:d-min-boost-gain-renamed-d-max-g.note: 4.3 renamed this setting to d_max_gain and kept your number, but retuned the boost. The same number now raises D from its minimum toward full D about half as much for the same gyro or stick activity, and the boost rises and falls faster. If D feels too low in propwash, raise d_max_gain.

upgrade:debug-mode-feedforward-names-ren.detail: The two entries were renamed in place in the debug table. 4.3.2 also added new debug modes such as D_LPF, GHST and RX_STATE_TIME.
upgrade:debug-mode-feedforward-names-ren.note: The feedforward debug modes were renamed in 4.3.2: FF_INTERPOLATED is now FEEDFORWARD and FF_LIMIT is now FEEDFORWARD_LIMIT. The name was updated for you, and other debug modes carry over unchanged.

upgrade:displayport-msp-lpuart1-renumber.detail: 4.3.2 renumbered the serial port identifiers: LPUART1 moved from 8 to 40, the new UART9 and USART10 took 8 and 9, and the maximum rose from 31 to 40.
upgrade:displayport-msp-lpuart1-renumber.note: LPUART1 is port 40 in 4.3.2 instead of 8, so a DisplayPort MSP port of 8 was changed to 40, which is the same physical port. Other port numbers carry over unchanged.

upgrade:dterm-lowpass-renamed-source.detail: Betaflight 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass_hz to dterm_lpf1_static_hz. It is the same filter, but the maximum dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz (LPF_MAX_HZ replaced FILTER_FREQUENCY_MAX).
upgrade:dterm-lowpass-renamed-source.note: Your static D-term lowpass 1 cutoff carries over unchanged under its new name, dterm_lpf1_static_hz, as long as it is 1000 Hz or below. The new maximum is 1000 Hz, so a cutoff above that turns the filter off (0), which is what the developers advise when you want less delay.

upgrade:dterm-lowpass1-renamed-max-1000.detail: In 4.3.2 this setting was renamed dterm_lpf1_static_hz and works the same way. The maximum lowpass cutoff dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:dterm-lowpass1-renamed-max-1000.note: Betaflight 4.3.2 limits D-term lowpass cutoffs to 1000 Hz. Above that limit, the developers advise turning the filter off to reduce delay. Your cutoff was higher than 1000 Hz, so this filter is now off (`set dterm_lpf1_static_hz = 0`). Check your filtering before you fly. To turn the filter back on, set a cutoff of 1000 Hz or less, for example `set dterm_lpf1_static_hz = 1000`.

upgrade:dterm-lowpass2-renamed-max-1000.detail: In 4.3.2 this setting was renamed dterm_lpf2_static_hz and works the same way. The maximum lowpass cutoff dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:dterm-lowpass2-renamed-max-1000.note: Betaflight 4.3.2 limits D-term lowpass cutoffs to 1000 Hz. Above that limit, the developers advise turning the filter off to reduce delay. Your cutoff was higher than 1000 Hz, so this filter is now off (`set dterm_lpf2_static_hz = 0`). Check your filtering before you fly. To turn the filter back on, set a cutoff of 1000 Hz or less, for example `set dterm_lpf2_static_hz = 1000`.

upgrade:dterm-lowpass2-renamed-source.detail: 4.3.2 renamed the gyro and D-term filter settings so they follow the same naming, keeping the same stored value. It also lowered the filter frequency limit from 4000 to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:dterm-lowpass2-renamed-source.note: This filter is called dterm_lpf2_static_hz in 4.3.2 and works the same way, so your value was carried over under the new name. The maximum is now 1000 Hz, and a value above that becomes 0, which turns the filter off.

upgrade:dterm-lpf1-static-max-1000-off.detail: The setting was called dterm_lowpass_hz in 4.2.11. Its maximum dropped from 4000 (FILTER_FREQUENCY_MAX) to 1000 Hz (LPF_MAX_HZ).
upgrade:dterm-lpf1-static-max-1000-off.note: This is your old static D-term lowpass 1 cutoff under its new name, and it keeps the same meaning. 4.3.2 accepts at most 1000 Hz, so a cutoff above that turns the filter off (0), as the developers advise when you want less delay.

upgrade:dterm-lpf1-type-renamed.detail: 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass_type to dterm_lpf1_type to match the gyro filter names, and added PT2 and PT3 to the list of lowpass types. The filter itself works the same way.
upgrade:dterm-lpf1-type-renamed.note: The first D-term lowpass filter type is the same setting under a new name, and PT1 and BIQUAD mean the same as before, so there is nothing to do. 4.3.2 also offers PT2 and PT3 if you want to try them later.

upgrade:dterm-lpf2-static-max-1000-off.detail: The setting was called dterm_lowpass2_hz in 4.2.11. Its maximum dropped from 4000 (FILTER_FREQUENCY_MAX) to 1000 Hz (LPF_MAX_HZ), and the default stays at 150.
upgrade:dterm-lpf2-static-max-1000-off.note: This is your old static D-term lowpass 2 cutoff under its new name, and it keeps the same meaning. 4.3.2 accepts at most 1000 Hz, so a cutoff above that turns the filter off (0), as the developers advise when you want less delay.

upgrade:dterm-lpf2-type-renamed.detail: 4.3.2 renamed dterm_lowpass2_type to dterm_lpf2_type to match the gyro filter names, and added PT2 and PT3 to the list of lowpass types. The filter itself works the same way.
upgrade:dterm-lpf2-type-renamed.note: The second D-term lowpass filter type is the same setting under a new name, and PT1 and BIQUAD mean the same as before, so there is nothing to do. 4.3.2 also offers PT2 and PT3 if you want to try them later.

upgrade:dterm-notch-cutoff-max-1000.detail: The maximum for this setting dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz (FILTER_FREQUENCY_MAX, later LPF_MAX_HZ).
upgrade:dterm-notch-cutoff-max-1000.note: The D-term notch cutoff means the same thing in 4.3.2, but the maximum is now 1000 Hz. A value at or below 1000 carries over unchanged. A higher value is lowered to 1000.

upgrade:dterm-notch-hz-max-1000.detail: The maximum for this setting dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz (FILTER_FREQUENCY_MAX, later LPF_MAX_HZ).
upgrade:dterm-notch-hz-max-1000.note: The D-term notch centre frequency means the same thing in 4.3.2, but the maximum is now 1000 Hz. A value at or below 1000 carries over unchanged. A higher value is lowered to 1000.

upgrade:dyn-idle-max-increase-renamed-mi.detail: In 4.3.2 the mixer update renamed idle_max_increase to dyn_idle_max_increase. It uses the same profile field and keeps the default of 150, but the minimum went from 0 to 10.
upgrade:dyn-idle-max-increase-renamed-mi.note: Your limit on how far dynamic idle can raise motor drive carries over under its new name, dyn_idle_max_increase. The new minimum is 10, so a value below 10 is raised to 10.

upgrade:dyn-idle-min-rpm-renamed.detail: In 4.3.2, idle_min_rpm was renamed dyn_idle_min_rpm. The units and meaning stayed the same, and the maximum was later raised from 100 to 200. 4.3.2 also stopped forcing the value to 0 when the RPM filter is off.
upgrade:dyn-idle-min-rpm-renamed.note: Your dynamic idle minimum RPM carries over unchanged under its new name. There is nothing to do.

upgrade:dyn-notch-width-became-count-n1.detail: The dynamic notch was rewritten to track multiple notches per axis, and SDFT replaced FFT. dyn_notch_count took over the slot of dyn_notch_width_percent, and the width logic was removed.
upgrade:dyn-notch-width-became-count-n1.note: Betaflight 4.3.2 has a new dynamic notch that tracks several separate noise peaks per axis, with one notch on each. A width of 0 ran a single notch per axis, which pilots usually chose to cut filter delay when the RPM filter handles motor noise. The number of notches is now set by dyn_notch_count, which stays at its default of 3 (range 1-5). If you want fewer notches, lower it, for example `set dyn_notch_count = 1`.

upgrade:dyn-notch-width-became-count-n2.detail: The dynamic notch was rewritten to track multiple notches per axis, and SDFT replaced FFT. dyn_notch_count took over the slot of dyn_notch_width_percent, and the width logic was removed.
upgrade:dyn-notch-width-became-count-n2.note: Betaflight 4.3.2 has a new dynamic notch that tracks several separate noise peaks per axis, with one notch on each. Your value set how far apart 4.2.11's two notches sat around one noise peak, and 4.3.2 has no equivalent setting. The number of notches is now set by dyn_notch_count, which stays at its default of 3 (range 1-5). Check your filtering before you fly.

upgrade:dyn-notch-width-percent-removed.detail: The dynamic notch was reworked to track multiple notches per axis, and dyn_notch_count took the place of the width setting in the same struct slot.
upgrade:dyn-notch-width-percent-removed.note: The old percent width of the dual notch has no equivalent, so nothing carries over. 4.3.2 tracks a number of notches instead, set by dyn_notch_count; check that value if you tuned the dynamic notch.

upgrade:dynamic-filter-feature-to-notch-.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the FFT dynamic notch with SDFT tracking of several notches per axis and removed DYNAMIC_FILTER from the feature list. dyn_notch_count sets how many notches each axis gets, and its minimum was lowered to 0 so it can switch the dynamic notch off.
upgrade:dynamic-filter-feature-to-notch-.note: In 4.3.2 the dynamic notch isn't a feature switch any more. You turn it off by setting the notch count to 0. If you had it off, it stays off with `set dyn_notch_count = 0`. If you had it on, it keeps 4.3.2's default notch count.

upgrade:f-pitch-max-halved.detail: The feedforward gain limit (F_GAIN_MAX) was cut from 2000 to 1000. The gain is still applied with the same scaling, so values within range keep their meaning.
upgrade:f-pitch-max-halved.note: The feedforward gain uses the same units in 4.3.2, but its maximum is now 1000. Values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and anything higher is capped at 1000.

upgrade:f-roll-max-halved.detail: The feedforward gain limit (F_GAIN_MAX) was cut from 2000 to 1000. The gain is still applied with the same scaling, so values within range keep their meaning.
upgrade:f-roll-max-halved.note: The feedforward gain uses the same units in 4.3.2, but its maximum is now 1000. Values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and anything higher is capped at 1000.

upgrade:f-yaw-max-halved.detail: The feedforward gain limit (F_GAIN_MAX) was cut from 2000 to 1000. The gain is still applied with the same scaling, so values within range keep their meaning.
upgrade:f-yaw-max-halved.note: The feedforward gain uses the same units in 4.3.2, but its maximum is now 1000. Values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and anything higher is capped at 1000.

upgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed-min-.detail: In 4.2.11 the stage-2 guard time was 200 ms plus failsafe_delay x 100 ms. In 4.3.2 the developers changed it to failsafe_delay x 100 ms with a 200 ms floor, to match Failsafe.md, and raised the CLI minimum to 2.
upgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed-min-.note: The number is kept, but 4.3.2 no longer adds a fixed 200 ms before stage 2 starts, so the same value now gives a guard time 200 ms shorter (e.g. 10 was 1.2 s in 4.2.11 and is 1.0 s in 4.3.2). Values 0 and 1 become 2 (0.2 s), the new minimum. If you want your old timing back, add 2 to your old number.

upgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed-min-.detail: To match the failsafe documentation, 4.3.2 dropped the fixed 200 ms that 4.2.11 added on top of failsafe_delay × 100 ms. It also set a CLI minimum of 2 (0.2 s).
upgrade:failsafe-delay-timing-fixed-min-.note: Your number carries over, but in 4.3.2 the same number triggers failsafe about 0.2 s sooner than in 4.2.11, because the delay is now exactly your value × 0.1 s. Values 0 and 1 are raised to the new minimum of 2. If you want the old timing back, add 2 to your value.

upgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-kept.detail: In 4.2.11 the recovery time was 200 ms plus failsafe_recovery_delay x 100 ms. In 4.3.2 the developers changed it to failsafe_recovery_delay x 100 ms with a 200 ms floor, to match Failsafe.md, and changed the default from 20 to 10.
upgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-kept.note: The number is kept, but 4.3.2 no longer adds a fixed 200 ms, so the same value now leaves failsafe 200 ms sooner (e.g. 30 was 3.2 s in 4.2.11 and is 3.0 s in 4.3.2), with a 200 ms minimum. 4.3.2 also uses this delay for every way out of failsafe, where some 4.2.11 paths used fixed times. If you want your old timing back, add 2 to your old number.

upgrade:feedforward-averaging-from-inter.detail: 4.3.2 counts feedforward averaging as the setting's value plus one, where 4.2.11 used the value itself. The final 4.3.2 names are OFF, 2_POINT, 3_POINT and 4_POINT.
upgrade:feedforward-averaging-from-inter.note: This value comes from your old ff_interpolate_sp, shifted by one step: AVERAGED_2/3/4 become 2_POINT/3_POINT/4_POINT, and ON (no averaging) becomes OFF. Old OFF, the non-interpolated feedforward, has no counterpart because feedforward is always interpolated now, so it also becomes OFF.

upgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-replaced-sourc.detail: In 4.2.11 the averaging count was the value itself. In 4.3.2 feedforward_averaging counts the value plus one, so old ON (count 1) matches new OFF.
upgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-replaced-sourc.note: This setting is now feedforward_averaging, with its values shifted by one step: AVERAGED_2/3/4 become 2_POINT/3_POINT/4_POINT, and ON (no averaging) becomes OFF. OFF, the old non-interpolated feedforward, has no counterpart because feedforward is always interpolated in 4.3.2, so it also becomes OFF.

upgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-to-feedforward.detail: In 4.3.2 ff_interpolate_sp (OFF/ON/AVERAGED_2/3/4) was replaced by feedforward_averaging (OFF/2_POINT/3_POINT/4_POINT), with the averaging count shifted by one. Old ON maps to new OFF and AVERAGED_N maps to N_POINT, but old OFF has no equivalent.
upgrade:ff-interpolate-sp-to-feedforward.note: OFF used the older feedforward calculation, without interpolation, and 4.3.2 removed that: feedforward always uses the new method, and its replacement setting only chooses how many points to average. The converter sets `feedforward_averaging = OFF` (no averaging), the closest match, but feedforward may feel different. If the sticks feel twitchy or noisy, raise feedforward_smooth_factor or feedforward_jitter_factor.

upgrade:frsky-spi-tx-id-rebind-required.detail: With FrSky ACCST 2.1 support, the stored transmitter ID grew from 2 to 3 bytes. The third byte is captured from the transmitter at bind time, and the D8 receive path now checks it. Older versions never stored that byte.
upgrade:frsky-spi-tx-id-rebind-required.note: 4.3.2 stores a longer transmitter ID for the board's built-in FrSky receiver, and your old binding is missing part of it. Your old ID can't be converted, so re-bind the receiver to your transmitter after flashing.

upgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped.detail: In 4.2.11 the value at index 0, shown as IMPERIAL, sent raw metric data, and METRIC applied the conversion. 4.3.2 changed the units enum to match the table (IMPERIAL converts, METRIC and the new BRITISH send raw data), so the converter swaps the label to keep the old behaviour.
upgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped.note: In 4.2.11 the frsky_unit labels were swapped: METRIC behaved as imperial and IMPERIAL as metric. 4.3.2 fixed the labels, so the converter swaps your label to keep the same behaviour on your radio. Nothing to do.

upgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped-2.detail: In 4.2.11, index 0 (printed as IMPERIAL) sent raw metric data and METRIC applied the unit conversion. 4.3.2 matches the code to the labels and adds a BRITISH option.
upgrade:frsky-unit-labels-swapped-2.note: In 4.2.11 the IMPERIAL and METRIC labels did the opposite of what they said. 4.3.2 fixes the labels, so your value was swapped to keep your telemetry in the same units as before. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:galileo-enable-behaviour-changed.detail: The u-blox setup code was rewritten when M9N support was added. Instead of writing a full constellation setup, it now reads the receiver's GNSS configuration and sets only the Galileo flag when it finds a default M8N configuration. OFF no longer actively turns Galileo off.
upgrade:galileo-enable-behaviour-changed.note: In Betaflight 4.3, ON turns Galileo on only when the GPS is a u-blox M8 receiver still at its default constellation setup. With any other receiver or setup, the receiver's own constellation settings are left alone. Nothing to do; if you want Galileo on another receiver, enable it with u-center.

upgrade:gyro-lowpass-renamed-source.detail: 4.3.2 lowered the static lowpass filter maximum from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz and renamed the gyro and dterm filter settings to match each other.
upgrade:gyro-lowpass-renamed-source.note: This filter is now gyro_lpf1_static_hz. It works the same way and is still set in Hz. Its maximum dropped from 4000 to 1000: values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and a value above 1000 becomes 0, which turns the filter off.

upgrade:gyro-lowpass1-renamed-max-1000.detail: In 4.3 this setting was renamed gyro_lpf1_static_hz and the maximum gyro lowpass cutoff dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz. The converter turns values above 1000 into 0 (off).
upgrade:gyro-lowpass1-renamed-max-1000.note: Betaflight 4.3 limits gyro lowpass cutoffs to 1000 Hz. Above that, the developers advise turning the filter off for less delay, so your filter is now off (`set gyro_lpf1_static_hz = 0`). Check your filtering: to turn it back on, set gyro_lpf1_static_hz to a cutoff of 1000 or less.

upgrade:gyro-lowpass2-renamed-max-1000.detail: In 4.3 this setting was renamed gyro_lpf2_static_hz and the maximum gyro lowpass cutoff dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz. The converter turns values above 1000 into 0 (off).
upgrade:gyro-lowpass2-renamed-max-1000.note: Betaflight 4.3 limits gyro lowpass cutoffs to 1000 Hz. Above that, the developers advise turning the filter off for less delay, so your filter is now off (`set gyro_lpf2_static_hz = 0`). Check your filtering: to turn it back on, set gyro_lpf2_static_hz to a cutoff of 1000 or less.

upgrade:gyro-lowpass2-renamed-source.detail: 4.3.2 lowered the static lowpass filter maximum from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz and renamed the gyro and dterm filter settings to match each other.
upgrade:gyro-lowpass2-renamed-source.note: This filter is now gyro_lpf2_static_hz. It works the same way and is still set in Hz. Its maximum dropped from 4000 to 1000: values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and a value above 1000 becomes 0, which turns the filter off.

upgrade:gyro-lpf1-static-max-1000-off.detail: The maximum went from 4000 Hz in 4.2.11 to 1000 Hz in 4.3.2. The developers' advice is that a pilot who wants less delay than 1000 Hz gives should turn the filter off.
upgrade:gyro-lpf1-static-max-1000-off.note: This value comes from your old gyro_lowpass_hz, which works the same way. The maximum is now 1000 Hz: values up to 1000 carry over unchanged, and a value above 1000 becomes 0, which turns the filter off.

upgrade:gyro-lpf1-type-renamed.detail: In 4.3.2 the gyro and D-term filter settings were renamed to match each other, and the gyro lowpass type list grew from PT1 and BIQUAD to PT1, BIQUAD, PT2 and PT3.
upgrade:gyro-lpf1-type-renamed.note: Your first gyro lowpass filter type carries over unchanged under its new name. 4.3.2 also offers PT2 and PT3 for this filter, if you want to try them.

upgrade:gyro-lpf2-static-max-1000-off.detail: When gyro_lowpass2_hz was renamed to gyro_lpf2_static_hz, its maximum dropped from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:gyro-lpf2-static-max-1000-off.note: A cutoff up to 1000 Hz carries over unchanged under the new name. 4.3.2 caps this filter at 1000 Hz, and the developers' advice for less delay is to turn the filter off, so a cutoff above 1000 Hz becomes 0 (off).

upgrade:gyro-lpf2-type-renamed.detail: In 4.3.2 the gyro and D-term filter settings were renamed to match each other, and the gyro lowpass type list grew from PT1 and BIQUAD to PT1, BIQUAD, PT2 and PT3.
upgrade:gyro-lpf2-type-renamed.note: Your second gyro lowpass filter type carries over unchanged under its new name. 4.3.2 also offers PT2 and PT3 for this filter, if you want to try them.

upgrade:gyro-notch1-cutoff-max-1000.detail: The maximum filter frequency in 4.3.2 dropped from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:gyro-notch1-cutoff-max-1000.note: In 4.3.2 the highest allowed value is 1000 Hz, so a value above 1000 is lowered to 1000. Lower values carry over unchanged. If you had a notch set above 1000 Hz, check its center and cutoff together.

upgrade:gyro-notch1-hz-max-1000.detail: The maximum filter frequency in 4.3.2 dropped from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:gyro-notch1-hz-max-1000.note: In 4.3.2 the highest allowed value is 1000 Hz, so a value above 1000 is lowered to 1000. Lower values carry over unchanged. If you had a notch set above 1000 Hz, check its center and cutoff together.

upgrade:gyro-notch2-cutoff-max-1000.detail: The maximum filter frequency in 4.3.2 dropped from 4000 Hz to 1000 Hz.
upgrade:gyro-notch2-cutoff-max-1000.note: In 4.3.2 the highest allowed value is 1000 Hz, so a value above 1000 is lowered to 1000. Lower values carry over unchanged. If you had a notch set above 1000 Hz, check its center and cutoff together.

upgrade:gyro-notch2-hz-max-1000.detail: In 4.3.2 the maximum filter frequency dropped from 4000 to 1000 Hz, and the firmware itself clamps the notch frequency to that limit.
upgrade:gyro-notch2-hz-max-1000.note: The second gyro notch now goes up to 1000 Hz at most. A value above 1000 was lowered to 1000, and anything at or below 1000 carries over unchanged.

upgrade:i2c1-overclock-to-clockspeed.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the on/off i2c1_overclock with i2c1_clockspeed_khz, which accepts 100-1300 kHz and is stored in the same I2C config slot.
upgrade:i2c1-overclock-to-clockspeed.note: The I2C bus speed is now set directly in kHz instead of with an overclock ON/OFF switch. OFF becomes 400 kHz and ON becomes 800 kHz, the speeds the old switch used, so nothing needs doing.

upgrade:i2c2-overclock-to-clockspeed.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the on/off i2c2_overclock with i2c2_clockspeed_khz, which accepts 100-1300 kHz and is stored in the same I2C config slot.
upgrade:i2c2-overclock-to-clockspeed.note: The I2C bus speed is now set directly in kHz instead of with an overclock ON/OFF switch. OFF becomes 400 kHz and ON becomes 800 kHz, the speeds the old switch used, so nothing needs doing.

upgrade:i2c3-overclock-to-clockspeed.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the on/off i2c3_overclock with i2c3_clockspeed_khz, which accepts 100-1300 kHz and is stored in the same I2C config slot.
upgrade:i2c3-overclock-to-clockspeed.note: The I2C bus speed is now set directly in kHz instead of with an overclock ON/OFF switch. OFF becomes 400 kHz and ON becomes 800 kHz, the speeds the old switch used, so nothing needs doing.

upgrade:i2c4-overclock-to-clockspeed.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the on/off i2c4_overclock with i2c4_clockspeed_khz, which accepts 100-1300 kHz and is stored in the same I2C config slot.
upgrade:i2c4-overclock-to-clockspeed.note: The I2C bus speed is now set directly in kHz instead of with an overclock ON/OFF switch. OFF becomes 400 kHz and ON becomes 800 kHz, the speeds the old switch used, so nothing needs doing.

upgrade:idle-adjustment-speed-removed.detail: The old integrating P controller was replaced by a PID controller with dyn_idle_p_gain, dyn_idle_i_gain and dyn_idle_d_gain, and its adjustment speed, P and P-limit parameters were removed.
upgrade:idle-adjustment-speed-removed.note: Nothing carries over from your old dynamic idle tuning. 4.3.2 uses a new PID controller for dynamic idle with its own gains, which start at their defaults. Retune them only if you had changed the old values on purpose.

upgrade:idle-max-increase-renamed-source.detail: 4.3.2 renamed idle_max_increase to dyn_idle_max_increase (default still 150) and raised its minimum from 0 to 10.
upgrade:idle-max-increase-renamed-source.note: This setting is now called dyn_idle_max_increase. It still caps how far dynamic idle can raise idle and has the same default, so your value carries over under the new name. The minimum is now 10, so a value below 10 becomes 10.

upgrade:idle-p-replaced-by-new-pid.detail: The old integrating P controller was replaced by a PID controller; dyn_idle_p_gain has a different range (1-250) from the old setting (10-200).
upgrade:idle-p-replaced-by-new-pid.note: Your old idle P value is not carried over. dyn_idle_p_gain is the P term of a new controller and is not the same quantity, so it stays at its default. Adjust it only if you want to retune dynamic idle.

upgrade:idle-pid-limit-removed.detail: The old P limit belonged to the integrating P controller, which was replaced by a PID controller with p, i and d gains and dyn_idle_max_increase.
upgrade:idle-pid-limit-removed.note: Nothing carries over from your old dynamic idle limit, and no setting replaces it. The new dynamic idle controller uses its own gains and dyn_idle_max_increase at their defaults.

upgrade:max7456-clock-options-redefined.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the HALF/DEFAULT/FULL options with HALF/NOMINAL/DOUBLE. NOMINAL is what FULL used to be, and DOUBLE (twice the rated clock) is new. The old DEFAULT ran the full clock and dropped to half only when the CPU was overclocked.
upgrade:max7456-clock-options-redefined.note: The OSD chip's SPI clock options have new names. Both the old DEFAULT and the old FULL mean the chip's normal rated clock, now called NOMINAL, which is also the 4.3.2 default. HALF is unchanged. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:pitch-rc-rate-default-changed.detail: 4.3.2 keeps the stored range at 1-255 but limits the value to 200 for the ACTUAL and RACEFLIGHT rates types. Separately, commit ad6885e1ee2e changed the default from 100 to 7, along with the new default rates_type of ACTUAL.
upgrade:pitch-rc-rate-default-changed.note: With ACTUAL or RACEFLIGHT rates, 4.3.2 caps this at 200: at boot the flight controller lowers anything higher to 200. 4.2.11 had no cap. With ACTUAL rates, 200 already means 2000 deg/s center sensitivity. With BETAFLIGHT, KISS or QUICK rates, nothing changes.

upgrade:rates-type-default-changed.detail: Commit ad6885e1ee2e changed the default rates_type from BETAFLIGHT to ACTUAL and changed the default rates with it (for example, pitch_rc_rate went from 100 to 7). The list of rates types and what each one means are unchanged.
upgrade:rates-type-default-changed.note: 4.3.2 defaults to ACTUAL rates, and its default rate curve is different too. Your 4.2.11 rates were kept, so your stick feel doesn't change. If you want to try the new defaults, switch to `set rates_type = ACTUAL` together with matching rate values: your current numbers mean something different under ACTUAL.

upgrade:rc-interp-channel-removed.detail: In 4.2.11, rc_interp_ch chose which channels RC smoothing applied to, in both FILTER and INTERPOLATION mode (default RPYT, all four). The 2021 rework of RC smoothing removed it and added no replacement channel setting.
upgrade:rc-interp-channel-removed.note: 4.3.2 always applies RC smoothing to roll, pitch, yaw and throttle, and you can't choose channels anymore. If you left throttle out to keep it as direct as possible, the nearest equivalent is a high manual throttle cutoff set with rc_smoothing_throttle_cutoff (0 means automatic).

upgrade:rc-interp-removed.detail: The rework that removed interpolation also removed the old check for whether smoothing was on. That check shows smoothing was off only when rc_smoothing_type was INTERPOLATION and rc_interp was OFF, so this setting's value is now carried by rc_smoothing.
upgrade:rc-interp-removed.note: RC interpolation is gone in 4.3.2. The only meaning that survives is rc_interp OFF together with rc_smoothing_type = INTERPOLATION (no RC smoothing at all), and that is now written as rc_smoothing = OFF. The PRESET, AUTO and MANUAL interpolation modes have nothing to map to, so those setups get the RC smoothing filter instead.

upgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-smoothness-spl.detail: In 4.2.11 the automatic cutoff (used while rc_smoothing_input_hz and rc_smoothing_derivative_hz are 0) was the rx rate / 2 x (100 - value) / 100, through a biquad filter, so the default of 10 gave 45% of the rx rate. The reworked RC smoothing in 4.3.2 uses PT3 filters, and its default of 30 gives 37.5% of the rx rate.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-smoothness-spl.note: 4.3.2 replaces this with two settings: rc_smoothing_auto_factor (setpoint and feedforward) and rc_smoothing_auto_factor_throttle. Both are left at their default of 30 because the same number now smooths differently. Higher values still smooth more, so adjust them if you want more or less smoothing than the default.

upgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-smoothness-spl.detail: The setting was split into rc_smoothing_auto_factor and rc_smoothing_auto_factor_throttle, and the smoothing maths and filter type changed, with the default moving from 10 to 30.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-auto-smoothness-spl.note: Your old smoothness number is not carried over, because the same number gives different smoothing in 4.3.2. The target defaults apply. If you want to change smoothing, set rc_smoothing_auto_factor and rc_smoothing_auto_factor_throttle yourself.

upgrade:rc-smoothing-merged-switch.detail: In 4.3.2 the CLI's RC smoothing report checks rc_smoothing = ON where it used to check rc_smoothing_type = FILTER. The new setting defaults to ON.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-merged-switch.note: In 4.3.2 this one ON/OFF switch replaces rc_smoothing_type and rc_interp. FILTER becomes ON. INTERPOLATION with rc_interp OFF meant no smoothing, so it becomes OFF. Interpolation no longer exists, so any other interpolation setup gets the default, ON (the smoothing filter).

upgrade:rc-smoothing-setpoint-cutoff-spl.detail: 4.3.2 split the single RC input cutoff into a setpoint cutoff and a throttle cutoff. Both keep the old 0-255 range and the meaning 0 = auto.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-setpoint-cutoff-spl.note: This setting takes your old rc_smoothing_input_hz value, and 0 still means auto. In 4.3.2 it filters setpoint (after rates) instead of rcCommand, and the filter is always PT3 instead of the old BIQUAD/PT1 choice, so the same number doesn't filter in exactly the same way.

upgrade:rc-smoothing-throttle-cutoff-spl.detail: 4.3.2 split the single RC input cutoff into a setpoint cutoff and a throttle cutoff. It also removed the rc_interp_ch channel mask, which decided whether throttle was filtered.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-throttle-cutoff-spl.note: This setting also takes your old rc_smoothing_input_hz value, and 0 still means auto. In 4.3.2 throttle has a cutoff of its own. Before, throttle was smoothed only if rc_interp_ch included it. Now it can't be left unsmoothed on its own.

upgrade:rc-smoothing-type-replaced.detail: In 4.3.2 the whole interpolation code path was deleted, and the INTERPOLATION/FILTER choice was replaced by an ON/OFF setting, with the filter as the only kind of smoothing.
upgrade:rc-smoothing-type-replaced.note: The ON/OFF setting rc_smoothing now carries this value. FILTER becomes rc_smoothing = ON. INTERPOLATION no longer exists: with rc_interp OFF it meant no smoothing and becomes rc_smoothing = OFF, otherwise you get the smoothing filter (ON).

upgrade:roll-rc-rate-default-changed.detail: 4.2 had no cap on this value. In 4.3 the default also changed from 100 to 7 to go with the new default rates_type, but the setting means the same thing.
upgrade:roll-rc-rate-default-changed.note: Betaflight 4.3 caps this rate at 200 when rates_type is ACTUAL or RACEFLIGHT: at boot, the flight controller lowers anything higher to 200. With ACTUAL rates, 200 already gives 2000 deg/s center sensitivity. Your value is kept, and with BETAFLIGHT, KISS or QUICK rates nothing changes.

upgrade:rpm-filter-min-hz-renamed.detail: During 4.3 development gyro_rpm_notch_min was renamed rpm_filter_min_hz, with the same default of 100. The lowest allowed value dropped from 50 to 30.
upgrade:rpm-filter-min-hz-renamed.note: Your RPM filter minimum frequency carries over unchanged under its new name. It still means the same thing in Hz, so there is nothing to do.

upgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered-8-to-4.detail: Betaflight 4.3 added UART9 and USART10 and gave them port numbers 8 and 9, so LPUART1 moved to port number 40. Version 4.3.2 rejects a `serial 8` line for LPUART1.
upgrade:serial-lpuart1-renumbered-8-to-4.note: Your LPUART1 serial port settings are kept. Only the port number changed, from 8 to 40, to match how 4.3.2 numbers this port. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:simplified-dterm-filter-off-for-.detail: While the slider is on, the Betaflight Configurator App locks the D-term lowpass fields, and moving the slider recalculates the static and dynamic lowpass cutoffs from 4.3's defaults.
upgrade:simplified-dterm-filter-off-for-.note: Betaflight 4.3 added a D-term filter slider (simplified tuning), on by default. You had set your own D-term lowpass cutoffs in this PID profile, so the slider is turned off here: your cutoffs stay as they are and you can still edit them. To use the slider instead, enter `set simplified_dterm_filter = ON`, but moving the slider then replaces these cutoffs.

upgrade:simplified-dterm-filter-off-when.detail: 4.3 added simplified tuning, and its filter sliders set the static and dynamic lowpass cutoffs. The converter writes OFF if any of dterm_lowpass_hz, dterm_lowpass2_hz, dyn_lpf_dterm_min_hz or dyn_lpf_dterm_max_hz was changed from its default. Otherwise the 4.3.2 default of ON applies.
upgrade:simplified-dterm-filter-off-when.note: You had set your own D-term lowpass cutoffs, so the new D-term filter slider is turned off. That way 4.3.2 keeps your values instead of recalculating them. To use the slider anyway, turn it on with `set simplified_dterm_filter = ON`, knowing it will then manage those cutoffs for you.

upgrade:simplified-gyro-filter-off-for-c.detail: While the slider is on, the Betaflight Configurator App locks the gyro lowpass fields, and moving the slider recalculates the static and dynamic lowpass cutoffs from 4.3's defaults.
upgrade:simplified-gyro-filter-off-for-c.note: Betaflight 4.3 added a gyro filter slider (simplified tuning), on by default. You had set your own gyro lowpass cutoffs, so the slider is turned off: your cutoffs stay as they are and you can still edit them. To use the slider instead, enter `set simplified_gyro_filter = ON`, but moving the slider then replaces these cutoffs.

upgrade:simplified-gyro-filter-off-when-.detail: 4.3 added simplified tuning, and its filter sliders set the static and dynamic lowpass cutoffs. The converter writes OFF if any of gyro_lowpass_hz, gyro_lowpass2_hz, dyn_lpf_gyro_min_hz or dyn_lpf_gyro_max_hz was changed from its default. Otherwise the 4.3.2 default of ON applies.
upgrade:simplified-gyro-filter-off-when-.note: You had set your own gyro lowpass cutoffs, so the new gyro filter slider is turned off. That way 4.3.2 keeps your values instead of recalculating them. To use the slider anyway, turn it on with `set simplified_gyro_filter = ON`, knowing it will then manage those cutoffs for you.

upgrade:simplified-pids-mode-off-for-cho.detail: While the sliders are on, the Betaflight Configurator App locks the PID fields, and moving any slider recalculates the gains per axis from 4.3's defaults (RP mode leaves yaw alone).
upgrade:simplified-pids-mode-off-for-cho.note: Betaflight 4.3 added PID sliders (simplified tuning), on by default. You had set your own PID gains in this PID profile, so the sliders are turned off here (OFF, or RP if you had changed only yaw, which leaves yaw editable): your tune stays as it is and you can still edit it. To use the sliders instead, enter `set simplified_pids_mode = RPY`, but moving a slider then replaces these gains.

upgrade:simplified-pids-mode-off-when-ch.detail: 4.3 added simplified tuning. Its PID sliders recalculate the P, I, D and feedforward gains per axis from defaults, and RP mode leaves yaw alone. The converter writes OFF if any roll or pitch gain was changed from its default, RP if only yaw gains were, and otherwise the 4.3.2 default of RPY applies.
upgrade:simplified-pids-mode-off-when-ch.note: You had set your own PID gains, so the new PID sliders are turned off, or set to roll and pitch only if just your yaw gains were custom. That way 4.3.2 keeps your gains instead of recalculating them from defaults. Turning the sliders back on lets them recalculate those gains.

upgrade:stats-switch-to-min-armed-time.detail: 4.3 replaced the stats on/off switch and its fixed minimum flight time with stats_min_armed_time_s. A value of -1 turns statistics off, and 0 or more turns them on with that minimum armed time in seconds.
upgrade:stats-switch-to-min-armed-time.note: Your choice to turn flight statistics on or off carries over. Off becomes -1. On becomes 10, which is the same 10-second minimum armed time 4.2.11 always required before a flight counted. You can now pick a different minimum in seconds if you like.

upgrade:telemetry-cap-used-sensor-disabl.detail: 4.3 made FrSky fuel reporting consistent. It added bit 20 (value 1048576) for capacity used, disabled that sensor by default, and raised the maximum from 1048575 to 2097151. Bits 0-19 keep their meaning.
upgrade:telemetry-cap-used-sensor-disabl.note: The telemetry sensors you had disabled stay disabled. 4.3.2 adds a new capacity-used (fuel) sensor, and the converter leaves it disabled, just as the 4.3.2 default does. To have it reported, subtract 1048576 from the converted value and set telemetry_disabled_sensors to the result.

upgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-new-b.detail: Commit d05d422bc0 added the capacity used sensor as bit 20, raised the maximum from 1048575 to 2097151, and added the new bit to the default set of disabled sensors.
upgrade:telemetry-disabled-sensors-new-b.note: In 4.3.2, SmartPort's Fuel sensor reports percent remaining (when a battery capacity is set) instead of mAh drawn. mAh drawn now has its own 'capacity used' sensor (bit 20), which stays off, as it does by default in 4.3.2. If your radio shows or announces Fuel as mAh, either use it as a percent, or turn the new sensor on by clearing bit 20 (subtract 1048576 from this value) and point your radio at it.

upgrade:thrust-linear-formula-rescaled.detail: The curve became a (1 - motor)^2 boost with throttle compensation and the maximum rose from 100 to 150. The setting also became per PID profile. 4.2.11 applied it from PID profile 1, so the converter writes it there, using a least-squares fit of the new curve to the old one.
upgrade:thrust-linear-formula-rescaled.note: 4.3.2 uses a different thrust-linearization curve: the same number gives about half the effect. Your value was scaled by about 1.8 to match your old curve (e.g. 40 -> 72). Values above 83 hit the 150 cap and come out slightly weaker. 4.3.2 also adds a small throttle boost at low throttle, so this is approximate: test-fly and adjust.

upgrade:thrust-linear-rescaled-1-8x.detail: 4.3.2 replaced the thrust linearization formula with a (1 - motor)^2 boost plus throttle compensation and raised the maximum from 100 to 150. It also changed the setting from a single master value to a per-profile value. A least-squares fit of the two curves gives a factor of about 1.8, and old values of 90 and 100 hit the new 150 cap.
upgrade:thrust-linear-rescaled-1-8x.note: 4.3.2 uses a new thrust linearization curve in which the same number gives roughly half the motor boost, so your value was multiplied by about 1.8 (capped at 150) to keep a similar feel. The setting is now separate for each PID profile, and your value went into PID profile 1, so set it in any other profiles you fly.

upgrade:vbat-pid-gain-removed.detail: VBat PID compensation was removed from the firmware in 4.3, and the old option was superseded by sag compensation. Its 4.2 default was OFF.
upgrade:vbat-pid-gain-removed.note: There is no replacement setting, so nothing carries over. If you had turned this on to compensate PIDs for battery voltage drop, you will fly without that compensation unless you set up sag compensation instead.

upgrade:yaw-rc-rate-capped-at-boot.detail: 4.3.2 added a range check to its rate-settings validation that caps the RC rate according to rates_type: 200 for ACTUAL and RACEFLIGHT, 255 for the others.
